what: satellite verifier validation: placebo (no repair claimed) and injected-change sensitivity
WARNING: There are no real repair labels, so this does NOT show the verifier finds real repairs. It shows how it behaves when nothing is claimed (placebo) and how large a change must be to be seen (power).
caveat: Random locations can contain real unrelated change (construction, vegetation), so the placebo detection rate is an upper bound on the false-alarm rate for 'no repair'.

outcome_split.reading: About two thirds of attempts on real ticket dates (April to August, so mostly monsoon) were cloud-obscured: a real limit of optical satellites in Mumbai. The read errors were ours: this run let three checks read six bands each in parallel and a quarter failed. The reader was fixed afterwards (a global cap of 6 simultaneous reads, 6 retries with backoff, a window-level retry, and failures are no longer cached); this run was NOT repeated, so the placebo below rests on only 23 measured locations.

limits_of_this_validation: Only 23 locations were measured, so the placebo and power estimates have wide intervals (placebo detection 13%, 95% CI 3% to 34%).
The injected-change power curve adds a known shift to the site's index differences; it shows sensitivity, not that real repairs look like that.
No real repair outcomes exist, so the likelihood ratios are not validated against real fixes.
Run before the reader fix and before the wording-based eligibility rule; the placebo samples all exact-location Mumbai points, not only large-area problems.
